claims.text: In donhang (kind 0.33, node image v1.34.11) the cluster DNS server is CoreDNS: two Pods in kube-system with label k8s-app=kube-dns, image registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.12.1, run by the Deployment coredns.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/coredns.txt; kubernetes.io: Tasks > Administer a Cluster > Using CoreDNS for Service Discovery

claims.text: The Service kube-dns in kube-system has cluster IP 10.96.0.10 on donhang, ports 53/UDP, 53/TCP, 9153/TCP; the client Pod's /etc/resolv.conf has 'nameserver 10.96.0.10'.
Port 53 is the DNS port; DNS can be carried over UDP (single messages, no connection opened) or TCP, which is why kube-dns lists 53/UDP and 53/TCP.
claims.source_hint: RFC 1035 §4.2 Transport (UDP and TCP on port 53); UDP gloss = foundation.l1.tcp-vs-udp claim 5 (verified, RFC 768); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/coredns.txt

claims.text: A lookup sent to kube-dns's cluster IP reaches a CoreDNS Pod through kube-proxy's rules, like any Service with a cluster IP.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Virtual IPs and Service Proxies; Customizing DNS Service ('CoreDNS Deployment is exposed as a Kubernetes Service with a static IP')

claims.text: The order of plugin lines in the Corefile does not set the order in which plugins see a query; that order is fixed when CoreDNS is built (plugin.cfg).
claims.source_hint: coredns.io manual: Configuration > Plugins (plugin chain order comes from plugin.cfg, not the Corefile)

claims.text: CoreDNS reads its Corefile from the ConfigMap coredns in kube-system (key Corefile).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Customizing DNS Service > CoreDNS ConfigMap options; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/coredns.txt

claims.text: Corefile syntax: a server block '.:53 { ... }' groups plugin lines in braces and serves the root zone '.' (every name) on port 53; each first-level line in the block names a plugin, and a braced block after it holds that plugin's options.
claims.source_hint: coredns.io manual: Configuration > Corefile, Server Blocks, Plugins

claims.text: The kubernetes plugin (zones cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa here) answers names under cluster.local; it watches Services and EndpointSlices through the API server and answers from what it has seen; a Service's name is answered with its cluster IP.
claims.source_hint: coredns.io plugins/kubernetes (Description: 'watches the Kubernetes API'); kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods > A/AAAA records

claims.text: No one writes a DNS record for a Service: the plugin answers from the Services it watches, so a Service resolves as soon as CoreDNS sees it, and once CoreDNS sees it deleted the name no longer resolves. Captured: echo-new resolves right after kubectl create service.
claims.source_hint: coredns.io plugins/kubernetes; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/coredns.txt (getent hosts echo-new... answers)

claims.text: 'forward . /etc/resolv.conf' sends queries for names not answered by earlier plugins (here: outside cluster.local) to the nameservers listed in the /etc/resolv.conf of the CoreDNS container.
claims.source_hint: coredns.io plugins/forward (TO may be a resolv.conf file); kubernetes.io: Customizing DNS Service (non-cluster queries forwarded to resolvers in /etc/resolv.conf)

claims.text: The CoreDNS Pods do not use the default (cluster) DNS settings; they are set to take the node's own, so their /etc/resolv.conf lists the node's DNS servers, not kube-dns, and forward sends outside names out; if it named kube-dns, CoreDNS would forward them back to itself.
claims.source_hint: coredns.io plugins/loop (kubelet passes the node's resolv.conf to Pods with dnsPolicy Default, 'this includes CoreDNS Pods'); kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods > Pod's DNS Policy (Default)

claims.text: 'cache 30' caches answers with a maximum TTL of 30 seconds, so a repeated outside name can be answered without asking upstream again; 'disable success cluster.local' and 'disable denial cluster.local' turn off caching of positive and negative answers for cluster.local.
The health plugin serves a health-check endpoint and the prometheus plugin exports metrics, here on port 9153.

show prints a command after '$' then runs it; coredns.sh rebuilds donhang (a kind cluster in Docker) if gone, saves the first echo-ip Pod's IP in pod_ip before the scale to 0, and its EXIT trap runs restore on exit, even after an error, scaling CoreDNS back to 2.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh and scripts/k8s/coredns.sh lines 10-15 at stage-3

claims.text: getent hosts NAME resolves a name through the system's resolver configuration (NSS, /etc/resolv.conf for DNS) and prints the address and name. wget -qO- URL sends an HTTP GET and prints the response body.
claims.source_hint: getent(1) and wget(1) man pages (-q quiet, -O- write document to stdout); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/coredns.txt

claims.text: With the coredns Deployment scaled to 0 and its Pods gone, 'getent hosts echo-ip' in the client Pod fails with exit code 2, while wget to an echo-ip Pod's address on port 8080 still returns its reply. echo-ip's Pods answer HTTP on 8080 with their name and the caller's address.

A Pod with the default DNS settings has only kube-dns in its /etc/resolv.conf, so a lookup of an outside name also goes to CoreDNS, and the forward plugin passes it on to the node's DNS servers; with CoreDNS down, outside names fail inside such Pods while the node still resolves them.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods > Pod's DNS Policy (ClusterFirst: non-cluster queries are forwarded by the DNS server)

claims.text: While CoreDNS is down, connections to addresses keep working, but every new DNS lookup from Pods with the default DNS settings fails, so programs that reach Services by name fail although their Pods stay Running.
The kubernetes plugin answers a headless Service's name with the addresses of its ready Pods instead of a cluster IP.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods > Services > A/AAAA records (headless); lesson k8s.l2.headless-services

beyond_scope: Plugin chain order fixed at build time, not by line order (one sentence, claim 5; asked by the junior review)
The disable lines of the cache plugin explained, since they appear in the Corefile on donhang
Housekeeping plugins health and prometheus named in one sentence; the other lines not explained
